chemicals.concentration_notes: Unripe fruit has the highest tannin levels; ripe flesh is the safest part. Even a single pit can be large enough to cause a gastrointestinal obstruction in a small animal like a cat.
chemicals.description: Persimmons contain no specific chemical toxin that causes systemic poisoning in cats. The main hazard from seeds and skin is mechanical (choking and intestinal blockage). The only chemical concern is tannins, which are concentrated in unripe fruit and can irritate the gastrointestinal tract.
chemicals.name: Tannins

description:
Persimmons are not highly toxic to cats, but they come with several health and safety risks. The main concern is the seeds and skin, which are hard and indigestible and can cause choking or a gastrointestinal blockage if swallowed. This is a mechanical hazard, not chemical poisoning.

Unripe persimmons are especially bad for cats because they are packed with tannins. Tannins are bitter chemicals that can severely irritate a cat's stomach, leading to vomiting, diarrhea, and intestinal inflammation. Even when the fruit is fully ripe, the flesh is very high in sugar and does not provide any nutrients that a cat needs.

A tiny taste of ripe, seedless persimmon flesh is unlikely to hurt your cat, but it should not be a regular treat. Always make sure to completely remove the seeds before letting your cat near the fruit. If your cat swallows a seed or eats an unripe persimmon and shows signs of stomach pain or vomiting, contact a veterinarian.

name: Persimmons
safetyNotes: Seeds and skin: hard and indigestible — choking and gastrointestinal blockage hazard; remove before offering any flesh
Unripe persimmons: very high tannin content causes severe GI irritation — vomiting, diarrhea, and possible intestinal inflammation
Ripe flesh: safe in very small amounts but high in sugar; no nutritional benefit for cats
Tannins can also cause intestinal obstruction by binding digestive proteins in large quantities
A tiny taste of ripe, seedless flesh is unlikely to cause harm; avoid making it a regular treat

symptoms.name: Intestinal Obstruction
symptoms.notes: The pits and skin of persimmons are hard, not easily digested, and are prone to causing dangerous physical blockages in the intestinal tract of cats. This is a mechanical hazard from a swallowed seed, not chemical poisoning.
symptoms.onset: Varies (typically develops over hours to a few days)

treatments.description: of the procedure: Contact an animal hospital immediately to inform them of the situation and transport the cat for professional emergency care. You should collect any remaining pieces of the ingested item (such as the persimmon or its pits) in a bag and bring it with you, as this gives the veterinarian a clear basis for making a diagnostic and treatment judgment34. treatments.name: Emergency Veterinary Consultation and Professional Care
treatments.notes: It is highly emphasized that you must not attempt to induce vomiting at home (such as by administering hydrogen peroxide) before speaking with a veterinarian, as this can be extremely dangerous with obstructive objects. Additionally, do not give the cat milk, food, salt, oil, or any other substances

treatments.description: of the procedure: Before heading to the vet, immediately move the cat away from the location of the food and clean up any remaining pieces to prevent further ingestion. Carefully check the cat's breathing and behavior to see if they are functioning normally34. Any situation-specific

treatments.notes: Ensure that children and any other pets in the household are kept away from the scene to prevent them from also ingesting the dangerous item
